name: Language Arts
topics: Some / Any · A few / A little · Too much / Too many · Enough · Simple past · Food containers

licoes.titulo: Nouns: people, places, animals and things
licoes.texto: A noun names a person, a place, an animal or a thing. (Substantivo)
pontos: Common nouns: any one of a kind: girl, city, dog.
Proper nouns: a special name. They start with a capital letter: Lis, London, Brazil.
licoes.fala: My name is a proper noun, so it starts with a capital L!

licoes.texto: A verb tells what someone or something does or is. (Verbo)
pontos: Action verbs: run, jump, read, swim.
Being verbs: am, is, are, was, were.
Théo kicks the ball. “Kicks” is the verb.
licoes.fala: I run, I jump, I kick! Verbs are the action of the sentence.

licoes.texto: An adjective describes a noun: color, size, shape or feeling. (Adjetivo)
pontos: a beautiful garden, a small cat, a happy day.
To compare two things, add -er: tall → taller.
To compare three or more, add -est: tall → tallest.
Short words ending in consonant-vowel-consonant double the last letter: big → bigger → biggest.
licoes.fala: An elephant is bigger than a mouse, and a blue whale is the biggest of all!

licoes.titulo: Simple past: things that already happened
licoes.texto: We use the simple past to talk about finished actions: yesterday, last week, in 2020.
pontos: Regular verbs: add -ed: play → played. Ending in consonant + y: study → studied.
Irregular verbs change: go → went, eat → ate, see → saw, have → had, run → ran.
Was with I, he, she, it. Were with you, we, they: The weather was sunny. We were happy.
licoes.fala: Yesterday I went to the park and played with my friends. Went and played are in the past!

licoes.texto: Most nouns just add -s: cat → cats. But watch out:
pontos: Ending in s, x, ch, sh: add -es: box → boxes, bus → buses.
Consonant + y: change to -ies: baby → babies.
Irregular: child → children, tooth → teeth, foot → feet, mouse → mice.
licoes.fala: One mouse, two mice! English plurals can be tricky.

licoes.texto: Every sentence starts with a capital letter and ends with an end mark.
pontos: . period: a telling sentence. ? question mark: a question. ! exclamation mark: strong feeling.
In English, these always start with a capital: names, the word I, days (Monday) and months (October).
Command: tells someone to do something: Close the door, please.
licoes.fala: In Portuguese we write “outubro”, but in English it is always “October” with a capital O!

licoes.texto: Synonyms have similar meanings. Antonyms have opposite meanings.
pontos: Synonyms: happy = glad, big = large, fast = quick.
Antonyms: hot × cold, early × late, full × empty.
Conjunctions join ideas: and (add), but (contrast), because (reason), so (result), or (choice).
licoes.fala: I was glad, which means happy, because we won the game!

questions.q: Complete: I have ___ bread in my bag.
questions.fb: Usamos some em frases afirmativas. “Bread” é incontável, então não usamos “a few”.

questions.q: Complete: We don't have ___ milk in the fridge.
questions.fb: Em frases negativas usamos any: don't have any, isn't any, can't find any.

questions.q: Complete the question: Do you have ___ eggs?
questions.fb: Em perguntas normalmente usamos any. A exceção é quando oferecemos algo: “Would you like some juice?”

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
opts: There is some cheese on the table.
There is any cheese on the table.
There are some cheese on the table.
There is a few cheese on the table.
questions.fb: “Cheese” é incontável: usa is (singular) e some na afirmativa.

questions.q: Complete: There are ___ apples in the basket.
questions.fb: A few acompanha substantivos contáveis no plural: a few apples, a few eggs, a few friends.

questions.q: Complete: I need ___ water, please.
questions.fb: A little acompanha substantivos incontáveis: a little water, a little sugar, a little milk.

questions.q: Which word goes with countable nouns like “cookies”?
questions.fb: Dá para contar cookies (1, 2, 3…), então usamos a few. Para leite, açúcar e arroz, que não contamos um a um, usamos a little.

questions.q: Complete: You ate ___ cookies! Your stomach hurts.
questions.fb: Too many vai com contáveis no plural (cookies, sweets, chips). Too much vai com incontáveis.

questions.q: Complete: This cake has ___ sugar.
questions.fb: “Sugar” é incontável, então usamos too much. E “too” indica exagero — mais do que deveria.

questions.q: What does “too much” mean?
opts: More than you need or more than is good
questions.fb: “Too” sempre indica excesso, algo negativo: too much salt, too many people. Já “enough” é a quantidade certa.

questions.q: Complete: We have ___ chairs for everyone. Nobody will stand.
questions.fb: Enough = a quantidade suficiente, nem pouco nem demais. Vem antes do substantivo: enough chairs, enough water.

questions.q: Which sentence shows a healthy habit?
opts: I drink enough water every day.
I eat too much candy every day.
questions.fb: “Enough water” é a quantidade certa. As outras mostram exagero (too much/too many) ou falta (don't eat any).

questions.q: Complete the question: ___ you eat breakfast this morning?
questions.fb: Para perguntas no passado usamos Did + verbo na forma base: Did you eat? Did she go?

questions.q: Which question is correct?
opts: Did you go to the park?
Did you went to the park?
Do you went to the park?
Did you going to the park?
questions.fb: Depois de did, o verbo fica na forma base: “go”, não “went”. O “did” já marca o passado sozinho.

questions.q: Give the short answer: “Did they build a house?” — Yes, ___
questions.fb: A short answer repete o auxiliar: Yes, they did. / No, they didn't.

questions.q: Give the negative short answer: “Did he help you?” — No, ___
questions.fb: No + sujeito + didn't. Lembre: didn't = did not.

questions.q: Complete: ___ she at home yesterday?
questions.fb: Com o verbo to be não usamos “did”. Para he/she/it no passado usamos was; para you/we/they, were.

questions.q: Complete: a ___ of milk
questions.fb: A carton of milk — a caixinha. Leite também pode vir em a bottle of milk.

questions.q: Complete: a ___ of bread
questions.fb: A loaf of bread = um pão de forma inteiro. Uma fatia é a slice of bread.

questions.q: Complete: a ___ of chocolate
questions.fb: A bar of chocolate = uma barra de chocolate.

questions.q: Complete: a ___ of jam
questions.fb: A jar of jam = um pote de geleia. Jar é o pote de vidro com tampa.

questions.q: Complete: a ___ of soup
questions.fb: A can of soup = uma lata de sopa. Can também serve para refrigerante: a can of soda.

questions.q: Complete: a ___ of rice
questions.fb: A bag of rice = um saco de arroz. Biscoitos vêm em a packet of biscuits.

questions.q: Which word is uncountable (não dá para contar um a um)?
questions.fb: Water é incontável — por isso dizemos a little water, nunca “two waters”. Os outros são contáveis.

questions.q: Which question is correct for uncountable nouns?
opts: How much sugar do you need?
How many sugar do you need?
How much apples do you need?
How many sugars do you want to count?
questions.fb: How much + incontável (sugar, water, rice). How many + contável no plural (apples, eggs).

questions.q: Complete: ___ eggs are there in the fridge?
questions.fb: “Eggs” é contável no plural → How many.

questions.q: What is the simple past of go?
questions.fb: Went. “Go” é irregular — não ganha “-ed”.

questions.q: What is the simple past of eat?
questions.fb: Ate. Outro verbo irregular comum na prova.

questions.q: What is the simple past of build?
questions.fb: Built — útil na unidade sobre casas: “They built a house.”

questions.q: What is the simple past of live?
questions.fb: Lived. Verbos regulares ganham -ed (ou só -d quando já terminam em e).

questions.q: Complete: Where ___ you live last year?
questions.fb: Pergunta no passado com palavra interrogativa: Where did you live?

questions.q: Give the short answer: “Were they at school?” — Yes, ___
questions.fb: Com o verbo to be, a short answer repete was/were: Yes, they were.

questions.q: What does a good paragraph usually start with?
opts: A topic sentence that says what the paragraph is about
questions.fb: A topic sentence abre o parágrafo e anuncia o assunto. Depois vêm as frases de apoio (supporting sentences).

questions.q: How do we start every sentence in English?
questions.fb: Letra maiúscula no começo e ponto final no fim — regra básica que vale nota na prova.

questions.q: Which words help connect ideas in a paragraph?
questions.fb: São os connectors: and (adiciona), but (contrasta), because (explica), also (acrescenta).
